common.tagline: Your tricking roadmap, from zero to expert

home.title: Learn tricking, level by level
home.subtitle: A clear roadmap from your first jumps to the most complex combinations. Track your progress locally and come back anytime.
home.feature1Desc: Eight levels ordered by difficulty, with a description of each stage.
home.feature2Desc: Each trick shows what you need to master before attempting it.
home.feature3Desc: Learn to chain tricks with smooth transitions.
home.feature4Desc: Your progress is saved on this device. No accounts, no tracking.

1.title: Fundamentals
1.description: Stance, straight jump, frog jump, guard, rolls, handstand, cartwheel, round-off, bounce and tuck jumps. All on the floor or mat, no high fall risk. The foundation everything else needs.

2.title: Air foundations
2.description: Pop 180 and the first front and back tuck rotations.

3.title: Flips
3.description: Front flip, backflip and gainer. You learn to rotate and land with control.

4.title: Spins
4.description: Kick 360, 540 and 720. Horizontal rotation enters the game.

5.title: Aerial kicks
5.description: Hook, round, push and crescent. Kicks that travel through the air.

6.title: Combos
6.description: Butterfly twist, tornado and aerial. You start mixing families.

7.title: Advanced
7.description: Double leg, full, double full and kip up. Multiple rotations and explosive exits.

8.title: Expert
8.description: Triples, sw9 and illusion combinations. The highest tricking repertoire.

stance.name: Stance
stance.description: Relaxed combat stance: feet shoulder-width apart, knees slightly bent, weight centered. It's the starting point and the return of almost everything.
stance.tips: Keep your feet parallel and your gaze forward. The weight should feel light, ready to jump.

fighting-stance.name: Fighting stance
fighting-stance.description: Variant with one foot forward to prepare kick entries.

ready-stance.name: Ready stance
ready-stance.description: Variant with lower weight, ideal to start a run or pop.

straight-jump.name: Straight jump
straight-jump.description: Vertical jump from two legs, arms up, soft landing in the same spot. You train height and landing control.
straight-jump.tips: Push with the whole foot, not just the toes. Land with bent knees to absorb.

tuck-straight-jump.name: Tuck straight jump
tuck-straight-jump.description: Variant bringing the knees to the chest in the air.

frog-jump.name: Frog jump
frog-jump.description: Jump from a low, almost crouching position, to train leg power.
frog-jump.tips: Load your legs as if you were going to jump over an imaginary fence. Hands touch the ground briefly on takeoff.

baby-frog.name: Baby frog
baby-frog.description: Frog jump variant with less height, ideal for beginners.

guard.name: Guard
guard.description: Defensive position with active hands, ready to block or attack.
guard.tips: Elbows in, hands at face height. Guard is trained like any trick: with repetition and consistency.

sweep-guard.name: Sweep guard
sweep-guard.description: Guard variant with a low sweep included.

forward-roll.name: Forward roll
forward-roll.description: Forward roll from stance, chin tucked, rounded back and hands protecting the neck. It's the safe base for any front landing and for all rotations.
forward-roll.tips: Round your back, don't force it straight. Chin to chest protects the neck.

shoulder-roll.name: Shoulder roll
shoulder-roll.description: Forward roll variant rolling over one shoulder, ideal to prepare lateral entries into flips.

backward-roll.name: Backward roll
backward-roll.description: Backward roll with legs going over, hips high and hands planting beside you to push the floor. You learn to roll over the spine without impact.
backward-roll.tips: Knees to chest, eyes to belly button. The squat is the starting point, not the end.

handstand.name: Handstand
handstand.description: Handstand with hands on the floor: aligned body, hands shoulder-width apart, fingers spread. Start against a wall and progress to freestanding.
handstand.tips: Push the floor away, bring shoulders over the wrists. The vertical line is earned with practice, not brute force.

handstand-wall.name: Wall handstand
handstand-wall.description: Handstand variant with feet against the wall to train the vertical line and shoulder strength.

handstand-free.name: Freestanding handstand
handstand-free.description: Handstand variant in freestanding balance, with no contact with the wall.

cartwheel.name: Cartwheel
cartwheel.description: Lateral rotation with hands and feet planting on the floor one after the other. You train inverted balance, coordination and line.
cartwheel.tips: The first hand sets the direction. Hips up, head neutral, second leg long.

cartwheel-step-out.name: Cartwheel step out
cartwheel-step-out.description: Cartwheel with a step landing instead of stopping, useful to chain with a run or pop.

round-off.name: Round off
round-off.description: Like a cartwheel, but you finish with both feet together facing forward, ready to jump or run. It's the natural hinge to front flips and twists.
round-off.tips: Block with the last hand, snap the hips. The controlled exit is half the trick.

round-off-step-out.name: Round off step out
round-off-step-out.description: Round off with a step landing, ideal to connect directly with another trick.

bounce.name: Bounce
bounce.description: Two-legged jump reused to chain tricks. The body goes up and down on the spot, keeping direction and tempo. It's the heartbeat of tricking.
bounce.tips: Springy legs, short arm swing. Train the bounce in sets, not in single jumps.

tuck-bounce.name: Tuck bounce
tuck-bounce.description: Bounce variant bringing the knees to the chest on every jump.

pike-bounce.name: Pike bounce
pike-bounce.description: Bounce variant with straight legs in pike position.

tuck-jump.name: Tuck jump
tuck-jump.description: Vertical jump bringing both knees to the chest in the air. You train the tuck position, which gives rotation speed in flips.
tuck-jump.tips: Grab the knees as you go up. If the legs don't reach, jump higher, don't tuck less.

pike-jump.name: Pike jump
pike-jump.description: Tuck jump variant with straight legs in a V.

straddle-jump.name: Straddle jump
straddle-jump.description: Tuck jump variant with legs in straddle position.

pop-180.name: Pop 180
pop-180.description: Jump with a 180 degree turn. Takeoff foot, head, shoulders and hips rotate together.
pop-180.tips: Start the turn with the head. Your gaze drives the rotation.

pop-180-step-out.name: Pop 180 step out
pop-180-step-out.description: Pop 180 variant with a step landing instead of stopping.

front-tuck.name: Front tuck
front-tuck.description: Front rotation with the body tucked to the chest.
front-tuck.tips: Grab the knees as you go up. Rotation speed comes from tucking, not from jumping higher.

front-pike.name: Front pike
front-pike.description: Front rotation variant with legs straight in a V.

front-straddle.name: Front straddle
front-straddle.description: Front rotation variant with legs in straddle position.

back-tuck.name: Back tuck
back-tuck.description: Back rotation with the body tucked to the chest. Your first big tricking jump.
back-tuck.tips: Throw the head over the shoulder. Jump up, not back.

back-pike.name: Back pike
back-pike.description: Back rotation variant with legs in V.

back-layout.name: Back layout
back-layout.description: Back rotation variant with the body in a straight position.

front-flip.name: Front flip
front-flip.description: Full stretched front flip. The back tuck and the pop 180 are its base.
front-flip.tips: Stretch hard the moment you see the ground. Hold the position until the last moment.

front-flip-step-out.name: Front flip step out
front-flip-step-out.description: Front flip with a step landing instead of stopping.

backflip.name: Backflip
backflip.description: The full backflip. Absolute tricking classic.
backflip.tips: Head back, jump up, open the chest at the end. The landing should be soft.

backflip-step-out.name: Backflip step out
backflip-step-out.description: Backflip with a step landing instead of stopping.

gainer.name: Gainer
gainer.description: Backflip with forward travel, useful for chaining and generating distance.
gainer.tips: The pop 180 sets the direction. Maintain height.

gainer-twist.name: Gainer twist
gainer-twist.description: Gainer combined with an extra twist.

kick-360.name: Kick 360
kick-360.description: Round kick executed in a 360 degree spin.
kick-360.tips: The support foot spins on the ball. The head marks the start and the end.

kick-540.name: Kick 540
kick-540.description: Kick executed during a 540 degree spin.
kick-540.tips: The kick is thrown in the second half of the spin to keep speed.

kick-720.name: Kick 720
kick-720.description: Two full rotations with a kick in the air.
kick-720.tips: Get the 540 solid first. The 720 is an extension of the concept.

kick-900.name: Kick 900
kick-900.description: Advanced variant of the kick 720 with extended spin.

butterfly-kick.name: Butterfly kick
butterfly-kick.description: Classic kick with legs opening and closing in the air. Style and flight.
butterfly-kick.tips: Hips start the movement. Think of kicking the air, not the ground.

butterfly-twist.name: Butterfly twist
butterfly-twist.description: Butterfly kick with an extra 180 twist.

butterfly-540.name: Butterfly 540
butterfly-540.description: Butterfly twist variant with a full 540 spin.

hook-kick.name: Hook kick
hook-kick.description: Hook kick traveling in an arc. Used in combos and transitions.
hook-kick.tips: The knee goes up, the heel describes the arc. Land with control.

hook-kick-twist.name: Hook kick twist
hook-kick-twist.description: Hook kick with an extra 180 or more twist.

round-kick.name: Round kick
round-kick.description: Classic round kick. The base of many combinations.

round-kick-twist.name: Round kick twist
round-kick-twist.description: Round kick combined with a twist.

push-kick.name: Push kick
push-kick.description: Front push kick, useful to keep distance or start combos.

push-kick-twist.name: Push kick twist
push-kick-twist.description: Push kick with an extra twist.

crescent-kick.name: Crescent kick
crescent-kick.description: Inside-to-outside arc kick, like a lunar crescent.

crescent-twist.name: Crescent twist
crescent-twist.description: Crescent kick with an extra twist.

tornado.name: Tornado
tornado.description: Combination of butterfly kick and 720 spin. Continuous, round movement.
tornado.tips: Chain the kick with the spin, don't separate them. It's one flow.

aerial.name: Aerial
aerial.description: Airborne rotation without hand support, usually with crescent or hook.
aerial.tips: Confidence is built with drills on floor and mat.

double-leg.name: Double leg
double-leg.description: Flip with legs in V position. Style and power.
double-leg.tips: Straight legs come up fast. The head stays neutral.

double-leg-twist.name: Double leg twist
double-leg-twist.description: Double leg combined with a twist.

full.name: Full
full.description: Backflip combined with a full rotation. Star piece of many combos.
full.tips: Feel the exact moment to start the spin. It's your most useful trick to chain.

double-full.name: Double full
double-full.description: Backflip with two full rotations. Advanced level.
double-full.tips: You need real height. Train the full until you make it automatic.

kip-up.name: Kip up
kip-up.description: From the ground, you push with your back and legs to stand up in a single move.
kip-up.tips: The head stays back; the impulse comes from the lower back and the legs.

kip-up-twist.name: Kip up twist
kip-up-twist.description: Kip up with an extra twist as you stand up.

triple.name: Triple
triple.description: Trick with three full rotations. Expert repertoire.
triple.tips: Only after many hours of full and double full in your body.

sw-9.name: SW9
sw-9.tips: Work on sw7 first if it's at your level. Fluidity is everything.

illusion-combo.name: Illusion combo
illusion-combo.description: Fluid sequence chaining aerial, full and kip up.

about.title: About Trickdex
about.subtitle: A personal, simple and honest guide to learning tricking.
about.whatIsBody: Trickdex is an open roadmap to learn tricking. It doesn't replace a coach, but it gives you a clear map of what to learn, in what order, and how to chain tricks.
about.philosophyBody: We believe in patient learning. Prerequisites aren't a hurdle: they're the shortest path.
about.dataBody: Your progress lives in your browser. There are no accounts, no servers storing your information. If you want to move it to another device, use export and import.
about.roadmapBody: The MVP is just the beginning. We have in mind a visual skill tree, a combo builder and, someday, a community. All in due time.
about.creditsBody: Made with care by b0nfire. The MVP media clips are placeholders.

footer.madeWith: Made with focus and lots of foam rolling
